author: From Staff Reports
title: BOYS BASKETBALL ROUNDUP: Region-leading Peachtree Ridge wins 6th straight - NewsBreak
text:
By From Staff Reports ,
6 hours ago Scenes from North Gwinnett boys basketball vs. Peachtree Ridge on January 28, 2026 in Suwanee. (Photo: David McGregor) By lmp SUWANEE — Peachtree Ridge extended its winning streak to six games and strengthened its hold on first place in the Region 7- boys basketball standings with a 74-67 win over Meadowcreek on Wednesday.
Tyler Barnes led four Lions in double figures with 25 points. Daniel Hollis had 19 points, Micah McMorris had 15 points and Duan Day added 10 points.
Peachtree Ridge improves to 15-8 overall and 10-2 in the region, taking a two-game lead on Meadowcreek (17-6, 8-4) and Berkmar (14-9, 8-4).
BOYS BASKETBALL
Archer 69, South Gwinnett 56
LAWRENCEVILLE — Archer knocked off South Gwinnett 69-56 in 4- on Wednesday.
Raheem Dyce led the Tigers with 22 points, David Simeon followed with 20 and T.J. Tunstall scored 14.
Berkmar 58, Parkview 56
LILBURN — Berkmar slipped past rival Parkview 58-56 in 7- on Wednesday.
Berkmar improves to 14-9 overall and 8-4 in the region, while Parkview drops to 13-9 and 7-5. The Patriots move into a second-place with Meadowcreek tie in the region standings, and Parkview falls into fourth place.
Berkmar was paced by Jayvon Rampersant (15 points), Chase Mohn (13 points) and Andre Sherrod (12 points).
North Gwinnett 73, Duluth 58
SUWANEE — North Gwinnett racked up 21 assists and topped Duluth 73-58 in 7- on Wednesday.
Micah Jones (19 points), Tristan Alusma (15 points, five assists), Max Patterson (13 points, five blocks), Connor Coxwell (10 points, four assists), Leighton McKinney (eight points) and Chauncey Davis (six points, five assists) played well for the Bulldogs.
Duluth was led by Jeremiah Anderson (24 points) and Malik Moore (11 points).
Hebron 65, Franklin County 60
CARNESVILLE — Hebron Christian notched a 65-60 win at Franklin County in 8-AA on Wednesday.
Devon McField (17 points, seven rebounds, three steals, two assists), Lukas Romine (16 points, 10 rebounds, three assists, two blocks), Zaiden Nelson (13 points, five assists, four rebounds) and Ashton Burt (nine points, four rebounds, two assists) stood out for the Lions (17-4, 7-0).
